Thermal Barrier Coatings (TBCs) have been used in high thrust aircraft engines for many years.
TBCs have proved to be very effective in allowing higher turbine inlet temperatures in aircraft engines.
TBC life requirements for aircraft engines are typically less than those required in industrial gas turbines.
The use of TBCs for industrial gas turbines can increase durability and longer service life.
The paper reviews early testing and applications of TBCs in industrial gas turbine engines.
The paper identifies and evaluates areas of concern from the engine designer's and materials engineer's perspective.
The key factors expected to influence the utilization of TBCs in advanced industrial gas turbine engines are discussed.
The goal is to produce reliable, durable, and highly effective TBC coating systems.
Improving engine efficiency and performance is the anticipated outcome of utilizing TBCs in industrial gas turbines.
The paper is focused on the perspective of TBCs for industrial gas turbine applications.
Solar Turbines Inc. is the affiliation of the authors.
The title of the paper is 'Perspective on Thermal Barrier Coatings for Industrial Gas Turbine Applications'.
The authors of the paper are Z.Z. Mutasim, L.L. Hsu, and W.D. Brentnall.
